**My thinking, as myself:**

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for as long as I can remember. I have about 8 mu under my household contract. I don't read much, but I know this land — I know when the soil smells right after rain, when the wheat leaves start yellowing from lack of water, and I know what my neighbors grow because we all grew up doing the same thing.

Around here, everybody plants winter wheat in October and then corn right after the wheat comes off in June. I'm not going to do anything different. That's what this land is good for. My mother did it, I do it, and that's what the soil and the weather here suits.

For wheat seed, I'll buy from the village seed station like I always do — whatever improved variety they're selling this year, probably Jimai or something like it. For corn, I always buy hybrid seeds from the market in town, because everyone says the hybrid gives more grain and I've seen that myself.

Fertilizer: I put down base fertilizer before wheat planting — compound fertilizer with some urea — and then I spread more urea in the spring when the wheat starts jointing. That's how my husband and I always did it. For corn I side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high.

Water: we pump from our well. Wheat needs water three times — once when it goes in, once at jointing, once at heading. Corn usually gets by on rain but I'll pump once if July is dry.

Pests: I spray herbicide after wheat emerges, and again at heading time for mildew and aphids. For corn I spray herbicide right after planting and watch for borer.

I'll plough the wheat field before planting — I like to turn the soil properly for wheat. For corn I'll do rotary after harvest, no time to plough.
